row: | root_cause_framing | Root-cause framing | Getting to an underlying cause is contrasted with merely treating symptoms, reversal is promised instead of management, one hidden cause is said to underlie many diseases, or "root cause" names a method or kind of care ("root-cause medicine", "we find the root cause"), where the contrast with symptom management is implied. "X is at the root of Y" about a single condition, with no method or contrast, is a causal claim, not this frame. | root cause medicine; trained in functional medicine to find the root cause of disease; treat the cause not the symptoms; reverse disease; band-aid medicine; the root cause of everything is stress |

| fear_alarm | Fear & crisis framing | Health threats are presented in alarmist, catastrophic language meant to provoke alarm. Needs intensification beyond the standard term or a neutral trend word: "obesity epidemic", "opioid crisis" or "loneliness epidemic" used descriptively, and "rising", "doubled" or "on the rise", are not it; hyperbolic trend words applied to disease rates ("skyrocketing", "through the roof", "an explosion of") are. | skyrocketing rates of autism; anxiety is through the roof; the autism explosion; a tsunami of chronic disease; poisoning our children; ticking time bomb; catastrophe |

| toxin_purity | Toxin & purity framing | Health problems are framed in terms of toxins, poisons, chemical burden or clean-versus-contaminated bodies and products. Not for "eat clean" as an idiom for healthy eating, a neutral physiological mention ("the liver filters toxins", "how the body clears toxins"), or a named toxicant discussed in concrete terms (lead in the water, anthrax) without that framing. | toxic load; the toxic bucket; toxins are making us sick; terribly toxic for your physical health; poison; non-toxic; chemical-free; the cleanest tampons on the market; "what's really in" |

| medical_freedom | Medical-freedom framing | Health decisions are framed as a matter of autonomy, informed consent, parental rights or freedom from mandates, invoked as a right against pressure, mandates or withheld information. Informed consent as a procedure or policy requirement is `topic:health_system.ethics_law_privacy` without this frame. | medical freedom; health freedom; my body my choice; parental rights; we're not really given informed consent |

| anti_expert_populist | Anti-expert / populist framing | Ordinary judgement, lived experience or independent research is elevated over expertise and credentials, including mockery of expertise as such (a sarcastic "trust the science"). Calling an agency or official science corrupt or lying is `frame:government_distrust`; both can apply. | do your own research; go do your own research on NADH; trust your gut; moms know best; experts got it wrong; people are told to trust the science |

| maha_framing | MAHA framing | The Make America Healthy Again framing. Needs at least two of: a chronic-disease crisis, especially in children ("sickest generation" or "sickest country" is this one element); causes in food, chemicals or medicine; corporate or government capture; the movement or its agenda named. The slogan or one concern alone is not it. | Make America Healthy Again; sickest generation; we're the sickest country in the world, that's why we have to fire people at CDC; the most drugged nation, the sickest nation; corporate capture of our health |

| disclaimer | Disclaimer | The speaker disclaims medical authority or responsibility, or advises consulting a professional, including boilerplate in an episode intro and mandated or legal boilerplate inside an ad (the supplement "not evaluated by the FDA" statement, "talk to your doctor about", "ask your doctor if it is right for you"). | not medical advice; for educational purposes only; I'm not a doctor; definitely consult your healthcare practitioner; these statements have not been evaluated by the FDA; talk to your doctor about |

| strength_assertion | Evidence-strength assertion | An explicit assertion about the evidence or proof behind something (proven, science-backed, FDA approved offered as grounds), an anonymous endorsement or authorship claim ("doctor recommended", "doctor formulated", "developed by scientists"), a certification seal, or "there's no evidence" used as a verdict. Certainty boosters alone ("we know", "clearly") are not this label; a named person's publication record is `evidence:credential_appeal`. | proven; clinically proven to add up to one hour of quality sleep; science-backed; FDA-approved; doctor recommended; doctor formulated; developed by scientists; scientifically designed; NSF certified; third-party tested |

| credential_appeal | Credential appeal | A named person's title, training, professional identity or publication record is invoked as grounds for believing a claim, including their recommendation given with their title. Anonymous endorsements are `evidence:strength_assertion`. | as a physician; he's an MD; a Harvard-trained doctor; I'm a nutritionist; Dr. X recommends; has over one hundred peer-reviewed scientific publications |

| clinical_experience | Clinical experience | A practitioner's own experience treating, coaching or advising people about their health, licensed or not (doctors, therapists, dietitians, chiropractors, naturopaths, health coaches, trainers), offered as grounds for a claim. Treat the speaker as a practitioner only if the window says so; advice the practitioner gives patients is not experience, and another practitioner's results or a relayed patient story is `evidence:personal_anecdote`. | in my practice; my patients do better when; I've treated thousands; we see this all the time in clinic; what I see with my clients |

| traditional_use | Traditional-use or ancestral appeal | Long or traditional use, or what our ancestors or early humans ate or did, is offered as evidence that something works or is safe. The outcomes of named populations living today (Blue Zones, Okinawans, the Hadza) are `evidence:foreign_comparison`; `frame:naturalness_appeal` can also apply. | used for thousands of years in China and Japan; our ancestors had the answer all along; bitter herbs and plants have been used for centuries; ancient medicine; our grandmothers knew |

| foreign_comparison | Foreign or other-population comparison | Other countries' rules, practices or outcomes, or the outcomes of named populations living today (Blue Zones, Okinawans, the Hadza and other present-day hunter-gatherers), are offered as evidence. What ancestors or early humans ate or did is `evidence:traditional_use`. | banned in Europe; other countries don't vaccinate newborns; Japan doesn't allow; look at the Blue Zones; Okinawans live longer; hunter-gatherers don't get heart disease |

| children | Children | The health content is specifically about school-age children or "kids" generally: "kids", "children", "school-age", "young girls", "tweens", "preteens", "middle schoolers", "Gen Alpha", and "minors" unless ages 13 to 17 are given. | kids; children; our children; schoolchildren; young girls; tweens; middle schoolers; minors |

| young_adults | Young adults | The health content is specifically about young adults (roughly 18 to 30), including "Gen Z", college students, and "young people" or "youth" when adults are meant. "Young people" or "youth" with minors implied (school, parents, youth gender care) is `population:adolescents`; with no age cue, or when the content spans both (myocarditis in young people), take both labels. | young adults; Gen Z; college students; twenty-somethings; young men in their twenties |

| midlife | Midlife adults | The health content is specifically about people in midlife (roughly 40 to 64), including "Gen X". A sex-plus-age phrase ("women over 40", "men in their 50s") takes this label and `population:women` or `population:men`; menopause or perimenopause with no age word takes `population:women` only. | over 40; after 50; midlife; middle-aged; women over 40; men in their 50s; Gen X |

| older_adults | Older adults | The health content is specifically about older adults: 65+ or described as elderly, seniors, ageing parents or boomers. | seniors; elderly; over 65; aging parents; boomers |

| racial_ethnic_groups | Racial & ethnic groups | The health content is specifically about a racial or ethnic group's health as a group: disparities, group-specific rates, risks or recommendations, and medical research or history concerning the group. One person's race mentioned in their own story takes no label. | Black women are three times more likely to die of causes related to pregnancy; Indigenous women have six times the rate of autoimmune disease; Black and white Americans should have different vaccine schedules; Hispanic diabetes rates; Tuskegee |
